h1: 3D rendering services London brands and developers can build campaigns on
intro: 22 Signals offers 3D rendering services. London is our head office. We make photoreal product renders, packaging visuals, interior and architectural CGI, and 3D models ready for websites and ads. Retailers, beauty brands, property developers and product companies use us when photography is slow, expensive or impossible because the product or building does not exist yet.

sections.h: When a photo shoot is the wrong tool
p: Photography is great when the thing exists, looks right and sits still. Plenty of London projects fail at least one of those tests. A beauty brand needs launch visuals before the first production run. A furniture maker wants every fabric option shown without making twenty sofas. A developer is selling flats in a building that is still a hole in the ground. A product company wants an exploded view that shows what is inside.
Rendering solves all of these. Once a product or space exists as a 3D model, you can show it in any colour, angle, setting or season, and change it next month without booking another studio day.

London adds its own pressures. Studio space is expensive, location permits take time, and launch dates are often fixed by a trade show, a retail buyer meeting or a sales suite opening. Renders take those variables off the critical path.

p: London uses more CGI than most people notice. The hoardings around new developments, the product images on a beauty brand's site, the furniture in a showroom brochure: much of it is rendered. Typical London buyers include:

UK consumer protection law and the ASA's advertising rules both expect visuals not to mislead buyers. For property, that matters a great deal. A CGI showing a park view that will be blocked by another building, or furniture that makes a room look bigger than it is, can lead to complaints and an ASA ruling. We work from architects' drawings and site information, and we add clear wording such as 'computer generated image, indicative only' where it is needed.

For products, accuracy matters for a different reason: returns. If the render shows a shade or texture the real item does not have, customers send it back. We match materials and colours to physical samples or supplier specifications, and we flag anywhere the render cannot be exact.

sections.h: How a rendering project runs: Talk, Plan, Build, Grow
p: Talk: a short call about what you need to show, where the images will be used and the deadline. Plan: we collect drawings, CAD files, samples or reference photos, and agree a written list of views, formats and dates. Build: modelling, materials, lighting and rendering, with draft views for your feedback before final quality. Grow: once the models exist, we reuse them for new colours, campaigns, animations and web 3D, so each new visual costs less than the first.
Your Signal Lead holds the schedule. Dates go in writing, especially for launch and sales deadlines.

We have worked with more than 30 companies across several time zones, and much of our visual work sits inside larger launches: a website going live, a campaign starting, a product reaching shelves. That is why we plan renders around the launch date rather than the studio's calendar.

Our head office is in London. You can bring samples, materials and drawings to a kick-off, and review key drafts in person against physical samples if colour accuracy is critical. Most review rounds then happen online with marked-up images.

Modelling and rendering run across our teams in several time zones, so heavy render jobs continue overnight. Developers and brands selling to buyers in the Gulf or the US can get versions styled for each market.

If you are pitching to a retail buyer in the West End or a property investor in Mayfair, we can also prepare a small set of hero renders first, so you have something strong to show while the full set is produced.

sections.h: Choosing 3D rendering services: London buyers' checklist
list: Ask to see renders of products or spaces similar to yours, not just a showreel

p: A render is rarely the final product. It goes into an ad, a website, a brochure or a launch video. Our 3D team works alongside our video, paid media and web teams, so the same model can become a product animation, a configurator on your site and a set of ad variations, without passing files between suppliers. Book a 15-minute call if you want to see whether rendering beats a shoot for your project. Related London pages: video production and animation, web development and paid media.

faqs.q: Can you render a product that has not been made yet?
faqs.a: Yes, that is one of the main reasons brands use rendering. We work from CAD files, technical drawings, prototypes or detailed reference images, and match materials to samples or supplier specifications. You get launch visuals before the first production run, and updates are easy if the design changes.

faqs.q: Do you do CGIs for off-plan London developments?
faqs.a: Yes. We produce exterior, aerial, street-level and interior CGIs from architects' drawings, plus show-flat visuals and floor plan graphics. We keep views accurate to the scheme and add indicative wording where needed, so marketing stays within ASA rules and does not mislead buyers.

faqs.q: Do 3D renders cost less than a photo shoot?
faqs.a: Often over time, though not always for a single image. The first render of a product takes modelling work; after that, new angles, colours and scenes cost much less than another studio day. For ranges with many variants, or products that do not exist yet, rendering usually wins.

faqs.q: Can the 3D models be used on our website?
faqs.a: Yes. We can optimise models for web viewers, product configurators and augmented reality, so customers can rotate a product or see it in their room. Our web team can build the viewer into your site, which avoids handing heavy files to another supplier.

faqs.q: How long does a set of renders take?
faqs.a: It depends on the number of products or views, whether CAD files exist and how complex the scenes are. A handful of product shots from good CAD data is a short job; a full development with exteriors, interiors and aerials is a larger one. We agree every delivery date in writing before work starts.

faqs.q: Can we review renders in person in London?
faqs.a: Yes. Our head office is in London, and for colour-critical work such as beauty or fashion we can review drafts in person against physical samples. Most review rounds happen online with marked-up images, and your Signal Lead keeps track of every change.

Yes. Because the model already exists, we can create product animations, exploded views, fly-throughs of buildings and short clips for social and ads. Our video and animation team works from the same files, which keeps the look consistent across stills and motion.
